analysis.title: CIO Flash Briefing: Midterm noise, year-end opportunity
key_insights: The CIO Office remains constructive on equities despite US midterm election noise and an AI-related sell-off, and keeps its overweight in equities.
Cost-of-living concerns drove the midterm shift in Congress and state elections. The war in Iran and AI infrastructure build-out both raised energy costs.

AI became a political target. New governors in Texas, Georgia and Ohio campaigned to pause or condition data centre approvals. Democrats now control states with more than 40% of planned US data centre capacity, which triggered an AI-led correction in equities.

The AI-stock drawdown began before the election. Investors questioned the viability of large capex plans and their funding needs. A September rates shock (first Fed hike since 2023, 10-year Treasury yield above 5%) stressed highly leveraged, debt-funded companies and shifted focus to hyperscalers with strong balance sheets.

The tech sell-off accelerated this week, concentrated in AI-related companies and less pronounced in the broader US market. European equities were much less affected. The correction is a rotation from AI stocks into defensives such as healthcare.

The bank reads the move as a healthy consolidation rather than the end of the AI investment cycle. Permissions and grid delays are stretching 2028 projects rather than stopping them, and 2027 capacity is largely locked in.

Major hyperscalers signed the White House's Ratepayer Protection Pledge, committing to pay the full cost of their power usage. The bank compares the situation to US railroad construction in the late 1800s, when farmer protests led to regulation without stopping construction.

Near-term uncertainty for the AI investment cycle will not dissipate quickly, and the bank expects continued volatility in the days ahead, particularly in tech. After that, seasonality and post-midterm patterns should support risk assets.

Sentiment has turned bearish very quickly and a rebound into year-end is possible. The bank stays constructive on the global economy into 2027, expects modestly slower growth, and says more defensive positioning may be appropriate alongside good diversification.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term volatility expected as the sell-off continues, but the correction is seen as consolidation and not the end of the AI investment cycle.
Defensive sectors such as healthcare are receiving rotation flows out of AI-related stocks.
Seasonality and post-midterm patterns should support risk assets, and the bank stays constructive on the global economy into 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The September rates shock stressed highly leveraged, debt-funded companies and shifted focus to hyperscalers with strong balance sheets.
The hike contributed to the pressure on AI-related capex funding and the equity drawdown.

risk_factors: Midterm election outcome and political backlash against AI data centre build-out, including state-level pauses or conditions on approvals.
Funding needs and viability of large AI capex plans.
Higher rates, with the 10-year Treasury yield above 5% after the first Fed hike since 2023.
Higher energy costs from the war in Iran and AI power demand.
